content.explanation: Higher testing levels demand more complete interrogation of the weld volume, achieved through additional angles, scans or surface preparation.

content.stem: In phased array, a sectorial scan is produced by:
options: Sweeping the beam through a range of angles from a fixed aperture
Moving the probe mechanically along the weld
distractors: Mechanical movement produces the encoded scan axis, not the sectorial sweep.
Firing all elements together gives a single unfocused unsteered beam.
Gain changes amplitude, not beam angle.
content.explanation: Electronic focal laws vary the delay across the aperture to steer the beam through an angular range without moving the probe.

content.stem: In phased array, a linear scan is produced by:
options: Stepping an active aperture along the array at a fixed angle
Sweeping through a range of angles
distractors: Sweeping through angles is the sectorial scan.
Rotation is a mechanical action, not an electronic scan.
PRF affects data rate, not scan type.
content.explanation: The active aperture is stepped element by element along the array, giving coverage along the probe without mechanical movement, at one angle.

content.stem: Electronic focusing in a phased array probe is achieved by:
options: Applying a delay law across the elements so the wavefronts arrive in phase at the focal point
Reducing the number of active elements
distractors: A curved wedge gives fixed mechanical focusing, which is not electronic.
Frequency affects resolution and attenuation, not focal position.
Fewer elements reduce the aperture and worsen focusing.
content.explanation: Delay laws are the defining feature of phased array, allowing both steering and focusing without changing hardware.

content.stem: Grating lobes in a phased array beam are caused mainly by:
options: Element pitch that is too large relative to the wavelength
distractors: Couplant excess affects coupling, not lobe structure.
Wedge wear changes the refracted angle and index point rather than creating grating lobes.
PRF affects data rate and can cause ghost echoes, which are a different artefact.
content.explanation: When the pitch approaches or exceeds a wavelength, constructive interference occurs at unwanted angles, producing grating lobes and spurious indications.

content.stem: Increasing the number of active elements in the aperture generally:
options: Narrows the beam and improves focusing
Has no effect on the beam
distractors: A smaller aperture gives a wider, more divergent beam.
Aperture size is one of the principal controls of beam shape.
Frequency is a property of the elements, not the aperture count.
content.explanation: A larger aperture produces a narrower beam and a tighter focal spot, improving lateral resolution.

content.stem: The steering range of a phased array probe is limited principally by:
options: The directivity of the individual elements
The length of the encoder cable
The thickness of the couplant film
distractors: Screen size is a display matter.
Cable length is a practical constraint, not a beam physics limit.
Couplant thickness affects transmission, not steering range.
content.explanation: Each element radiates over a limited angular range, so steering far from normal loses sensitivity even though the focal law is valid.

content.stem: An encoder is used in phased array weld inspection to:
options: Relate collected data to position along the weld
distractors: Angle range is set by the focal laws and probe.
Attenuation is a material property.
Calibration blocks are still required.
content.explanation: Positional encoding is what makes the data reviewable and re examinable, and it is normally required for coded PAUT.

content.stem: Under ISO 13588, encoded data is generally required because:
options: It permits later review and demonstrates coverage
It is faster than manual scanning
It removes the need for personnel certification
It eliminates the need for a procedure
distractors: Speed is a benefit but not the reason the standard requires encoding.
Certification to ISO 9712 is still required.
A written procedure is still required.
content.explanation: The auditable record of position and amplitude is the main advantage of automated phased array over manual ultrasonics.

content.stem: Verification that all elements of a phased array probe are active is normally performed by:
options: An element activity check against a reference reflector or backwall
distractors: Lux meters belong to surface method viewing conditions.
Settlement tests belong to magnetic particle ink control.
Densitometers belong to radiography.
content.explanation: Element activity checks fire each element in turn and compare its response, revealing dead or weak elements before they cause missed coverage.

content.stem: Under ISO 18563-3, the maximum number of inactive elements normally tolerated in an array is stated because:
options: Dead elements distort the beam and reduce sensitivity
distractors: Element condition does not change frequency.
Cable life is unrelated.
Acceptance levels are fixed by standard.
content.explanation: A dead element changes the aperture and distorts the focal law, so a limit is set and exceeding it takes the probe out of service.

content.stem: A time corrected gain calibration in phased array serves to:
options: Equalise the response from equal reflectors at different depths
distractors: Angle is set by the focal law.
Wedge delay is a separate calibration.
Pitch is a fixed probe property.
content.explanation: TCG applies depth dependent gain so a given reflector gives the same amplitude regardless of sound path, which is essential for amplitude based acceptance.

content.stem: Angle corrected gain in phased array is required because:
options: Sensitivity varies with steering angle across a sectorial scan
The encoder resolution changes with angle
distractors: Thickness variation is handled by the scan plan and TCG.
Couplant does not vary with beam angle.
Encoder resolution is independent of beam angle.
content.explanation: Element directivity and wedge attenuation vary across the sweep, so ACG equalises the response at each angle.

content.stem: A scan plan for phased array weld inspection must demonstrate:
options: That the beams cover the weld volume and both fusion faces
The paint system to be applied
distractors: Cost is a commercial matter.
Welder qualification is a welding record.
Coating is unrelated.
content.explanation: Coverage is the central claim of a phased array examination, and the scan plan is the evidence that the focal laws reach every part of the weld.

content.stem: Under ISO 13588, where full coverage cannot be achieved the correct action is to:
options: Record the untested volume and report it
Report the weld as fully tested
distractors: Claiming full coverage where it was not achieved is a false record.
Gain does not create coverage where no beam reaches.
Acceptance levels are not adjusted for access limitations.
content.explanation: Honest recording of the untested volume is required so that the limitation is visible to the reader and can be addressed by other means.

content.stem: In phased array data, an S scan display shows:
options: Amplitude against angle and sound path from one probe position
Position along the weld against depth for one angle
The raw radio frequency waveform only
distractors: Amplitude against time alone is the A scan.
Position against depth for one angle is closer to a B scan.
The raw waveform is the A scan signal.
content.explanation: The sectorial or S scan plots the swept angular range as a fan, showing where in the cross section each indication lies.

content.stem: A C scan display in phased array presents:
options: A plan view of the component with amplitude or depth mapped over the surface
A cross sectional fan of angles
distractors: A single waveform is the A scan.
The angular fan is the S scan.
Focal laws are set up data, not a display.
content.explanation: The C scan is the top view, showing extent of indications over the scanned area, which is why it is used for sizing length.

content.stem: Sizing the through wall extent of a planar flaw by phased array is most reliably done by:
options: A tip diffraction or similar geometric technique rather than amplitude alone
Counting the number of active elements
distractors: Peak amplitude sizing underestimates unfavourably oriented planar flaws.
Element count is an equipment parameter.
Encoder distance gives length along the weld, not through wall extent.
content.explanation: Amplitude responses depend strongly on orientation, so diffraction based sizing is preferred for through wall extent of planar flaws.

content.stem: Time of flight diffraction is often combined with phased array because:
options: It sizes through wall extent well and is relatively orientation insensitive
It removes the need for an encoder
distractors: TOFD calibration is not inherently quicker.
Couplant is required for TOFD as for any contact ultrasonic method.
TOFD is normally encoded as well.
content.explanation: TOFD relies on diffracted signals from flaw tips, which are less dependent on orientation than the specular reflections phased array relies on.

content.stem: Time of flight diffraction is specified for welds in:
distractors: ISO 13588 covers phased array technique.
ISO 19285 gives phased array acceptance levels.
ISO 22825 covers ultrasonic testing of austenitic welds.
content.explanation: ISO 10863 covers the use of TOFD for welds, with ISO 15626 giving the acceptance levels.

content.stem: Acceptance levels for time of flight diffraction of welds are given in:
distractors: ISO 10863 is the TOFD technique standard.
ISO 19285 covers phased array.
ISO 11666 covers conventional ultrasonic testing.
content.explanation: ISO 15626 gives the TOFD acceptance levels, matching the pattern of a technique standard plus an acceptance standard for each method.

content.stem: The lateral wave in a TOFD setup travels:
options: Along the surface between transmitter and receiver
Through the full thickness and back
Around the circumference of the pipe
distractors: The full thickness path gives the backwall signal.
Circumferential travel is not the lateral wave.
Wedge travel is the wedge delay, removed by calibration.
content.explanation: The lateral wave is the first arrival, travelling just under the surface, and its loss or disturbance signals a near surface flaw.

content.stem: A dead zone exists near the scanning surface in TOFD because:
options: The lateral wave masks signals arriving at nearly the same time
The encoder cannot resolve that region
The couplant is too thick there
Phased array focal laws do not reach it
distractors: The encoder measures position along the weld, not depth.
Couplant thickness is not the cause.
The dead zone is a TOFD limitation, not a phased array one.
content.explanation: The finite duration of the lateral wave obscures the arrival of tip signals from very shallow flaws, which is why TOFD is normally combined with a surface or phased array technique.

content.stem: Under ISO 19285, acceptance of an indication is based on:
options: Amplitude relative to the reference level together with length limits
distractors: Amplitude alone would permit long low level indications.
Length alone would permit short high amplitude planar flaws.
Certification governs who may evaluate, not the criteria.
content.explanation: As with conventional ultrasonics, both the echo height relative to the reference and the extent of the indication are assessed.

content.stem: Under the ISO phased array acceptance standards, a flaw characterised as planar is:
options: Assessed only at testing level D
distractors: Length allowances apply to volumetric indications.
A low amplitude does not make a crack acceptable.
Testing level governs coverage, not acceptance criteria.
content.explanation: As in ISO 11666, planar imperfections such as cracks and lack of fusion are not tolerated, which makes characterisation important.

content.stem: The reference block used to set sensitivity for phased array weld inspection normally contains:
options: Side drilled holes at a range of depths
distractors: A single backwall gives one depth point and cannot define a curve.
The quadrant of the V1 block is used for angle and index point work, not TCG.
Wire IQIs are radiographic devices.
content.explanation: Side drilled holes at several depths allow a TCG curve to be built across the sound path range of interest.

content.stem: Wedge delay calibration in phased array corrects for:
options: The time the sound spends in the wedge before entering the part
distractors: Material attenuation is addressed by TCG and transfer correction.
Encoder step is a scan parameter.
Temperature affects wedge velocity, which is why the check is repeated, but the calibration itself removes the transit time.
content.explanation: Wedge delay removes the fixed transit time in the wedge so that depths read correctly, and it must be repeated for each focal law group.

content.stem: Under ISO 13588, in service checks of the phased array system during a shift typically include:
options: Sensitivity and element activity verification against the reference block
A hardness test on the weld
A dye penetrant check of the wedge
distractors: Hardness testing is a separate mechanical test.
Penetrant testing of a plastic wedge is not meaningful.
Radiography is a different method entirely.
content.explanation: Checks that the system still responds as calibrated, and that no element has failed, protect the validity of the shift's data.

content.stem: The written phased array procedure required by ISO 13588 shall be approved by:
options: A Level 3 qualified in the method
distractors: A Level 2 may write instructions from an approved procedure but does not approve it.
Site management does not hold method authority.
Equipment suppliers do not approve procedures.
content.explanation: Procedure approval is a Level 3 responsibility under ISO 9712, including the scan plan that demonstrates coverage.

content.stem: Under ISO 9712, phased array ultrasonic testing is:
options: A technique within the ultrasonic method, certified with a stated scope
A separate method with its own experience table
distractors: It sits under the ultrasonic method rather than having a separate table.
Personnel certification applies to it as to any technique.
It is certified at Levels 1, 2 and 3 as applicable.
content.explanation: ISO 9712 treats PAUT as a UT technique, and certification schemes such as PCN issue it as a defined scope within ultrasonics.

content.stem: A PCN candidate seeking phased array certification would normally be required to hold or demonstrate:
options: Competence in conventional ultrasonic testing as a foundation
distractors: Radiography is an unrelated method.
Welding qualification is not a prerequisite for NDT certification.
Coating inspection is unrelated.
content.explanation: Phased array builds on conventional ultrasonic principles, so schemes require an ultrasonic foundation before the phased array scope.

content.stem: In a PCN phased array practical examination, the candidate would be expected to:
options: Build and justify a scan plan, calibrate, scan, and evaluate encoded data
Watch an examiner perform the scan
Submit a portfolio of past reports
distractors: Theory is examined in the general and specific papers.
Observation is training, not examination.
Past reports evidence experience, not competence under examination.
content.explanation: The practical examination tests the full chain from scan plan through calibration and scanning to evaluation and reporting.

content.stem: Phased array inspection of austenitic welds is difficult principally because:
options: Anisotropic coarse grain structure refracts and attenuates the beam
Encoders do not work on stainless steel
distractors: Magnetic properties matter to magnetic particle testing, not ultrasonics.
Couplant works normally on stainless steel.
Encoders function normally; magnetic wheel encoders need an alternative fixing.
content.explanation: The columnar grain structure bends and scatters the beam so the actual beam path differs from the focal law prediction.

content.stem: Under ISO 13588, the data recorded for later review shall include:
options: Position, amplitude and time or depth information for the scanned volume
Only the indications the operator chose to save
distractors: Saving only selected indications defeats the purpose of encoded data.
A photograph is not ultrasonic data.
Certification is recorded in the report but is not scan data.
content.explanation: The complete data set is what allows independent review, which is the reason coded phased array is specified.

content.stem: The phased array report required under the ISO family shall state the testing level and scan plan reference because:
options: They define the coverage achieved and allow the result to be judged
distractors: Dose belongs to radiography.
Dwell belongs to penetrant testing.
Magnetising current belongs to magnetic particle testing.
content.explanation: Without the testing level and scan plan the reader cannot know what volume was interrogated.
